top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Hanson, Katz) pairs a mature framework for how technology shifts labour demand and the wage structure with transparent local-labour-market designs for import competition. The work spans about three decades, has been replicated and criticised across countries, and the live disputes concern magnitude and persistence rather than existence. I rank it above P002 because the citation covers labour demand and wage structure broadly, which needs Katz's independent skill-premium work to explain why the trade evidence bears on labour demand and not only on local adjustment. The citation should not claim origination of the task framework or restate the 2023 and 2024 prizes. Katz is the most exposed name because of the overlap with Goldin, and Dorn's exclusion is a real cost of the three-name cap. P002 is a close second and defensible as a single design-based discovery, and I rank it above no award because the achievement is mature and prize-worthy either way. Ten members' agreement is convergence, not evidence of merit, and I have not counted it as such.
recusal_note: No tie to Autor, Hanson, Katz or Dorn is apparent from my profile. I disclose co-authorship and IIES colleagueship with Krusell (secretary) and Hassler (chair), who also support P001, so their agreement is not independent confirmation of my view. I also disclose field proximity in growth, structural change and labour reallocation. Not adjudicated.
